newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals on Tuesday put a damper on expectations of an early cut in Bank rate, saying it would be later rather than sooner, "with the emphasis on later".

- Standard Bank Investment Holdings Ltd reported a 27 percent increase in net profit to 1.55 billion rand on Tuesday, benefiting from increases in non-interest income and an increased contribution from associates for the financial year to the end of December.

- First National Bank Holdings Ltd will face a long delayed civil court action next month over allegations that FNB management, including managing director Viv Bartlett, knew that engineering firm KPL Etsa had traded recklessly several months before it was liquidated.

- A major clean-out of the South African National Defence Force's (SANDF) top structures, which will see SANDF chief Georg Meiring stripped of his financial powers and other senior officers retrenched or retired, was announced by Deputy Defence Minister Ronnie Kasrils on Tuesday.
BUSINESS REPORT

- NBS Holdings Ltd and Boland Bank Holdings Ltd will merge on April 1, creating South Africa's fifth-largest banking group with combined total assets of R26.5 billion, the banks said on Tuesday. The bank will be listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange as NBS Boland Limited.

- The Reserve Bank sent out confusing signals on Tuesday, causing the rand to suffer its biggest one-day fall of the year, dealers said. The unit tumbled more than three cents to reach R4.4395 in late trade.
- The U.S. was challenging South Africa's position as the world's foremost gold producer, the U.S. Gold Institute said this week.
- Attempts by the Mpumalanga provincial government to end the controversy surrounding the Dolphin deal by appointing an investigative committee backfired on Tuesday.
SAKE BEELD

- Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals brought the rand's strong run of the past few weeks to a halt on Tuesday after he told an international press conference that the currency's gains had been slightly overdone.
- Economic fundamentals have in recent times improved and already early in the new year there is a spirit of optimism that the economy will stabilise this year, Stals said on Tuesday.
- The government on Tuesday announced a number of steps to speed up and expand the restructure and privatisation of state assets.
- Standard Bank increased earnings in the year to end-December 1996 by 27 percent to 1.55 billion rand.
THE STAR
- Opposition parties warned on Tuesday that the country was sliding towards anarchy and urged the government to get tougher on crime.

- The high-flying rand fell to earth with a thud on Tuesday after Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals' comments that the South African currency's recovery from last year's depths may be an "over adjustment".
